what_happened: Research found that the task description's implicit premise (per-repo-scoping.md's claim that the transcript-capture path 'cannot be fixed from this repository') is outdated: it described upload.py's dead code path, not the live extract_local.py pipeline, which exposes a fixable pre-review provenance-injection point in pending_kos.jsonl (a ledger file preserved across vendor auto-updates).

Premise re-validation confirmed every live-checkable carried figure exactly (1260 nvim pending of 3757 total; 0 of 3757 records carry a provenance key; capture.projects nvim -> /home/benjamin/.config/nvim), so no plan phase had to hedge against a stale premise.

The shared resolve_checkout_toplevel block's own in-block comment names five copies while the lockstep guard (Case 30 in test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh) enumerates eight. Because the guard compares byte-for-byte, a ninth copy must reproduce the stale comment verbatim and must not be corrected in one copy alone -- recorded as a Phase 1 risk in the plan.

Two phases independently edit manifest.json's provides.scripts, and validate-artifact.sh's suite-selection check showed that surface maps to ~37 suites corpus-wide, so no run-all.sh --only narrowing covers it. Both phases were therefore raised from local to full with the cross-cutting surface named, rather than naming a suite list that would have fabricated coverage.

Phase 1's scoped batch-gate discharge attempt (verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 8 --gate8-touched <new script path>,manifest.json --skip-unchanged) hit the UNMAPPABLE touched-path case: sapience-tag-pending.sh is a brand-new file with no covering test suite yet (Phase 2 creates test-sapience-tag-pending.sh next in this same dispatch), so suite_selection_select returned the full-sweep sentinel and verify-deploy.sh fell back to the complete unnarrowed run-all.sh battery under heavy multi-task batch contention (gate-lock host mutex reclaimed as stale from another session, 1-minute load average 6.25, overall run-all.sh reported FAIL on undiscoverable/failing suites). Per the dispatch's UNMAPPABLE CRITERION carve-out, pivoted to running the two named checks Phase 1's own Tier Justification identifies (test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh, test-script-inventory.sh) directly and standalone instead of re-attempting the full sweep.

First deploy-headless.sh run in Phase 4 failed verification: check-extension-docs.sh's Rule U (EXTENSION.md 60-line limit) flagged the sapience EXTENSION.md edit from Phase 3 at 63 lines. Trimmed the 'What this extension adds' paragraph back to 6 lines (60 total) while keeping the new script named with its role; re-ran deploy-headless.sh, which then passed all 41 checks.

Phase 4's verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 8 --gate8-touched <task's touched paths> --skip-unchanged narrowed correctly to 34 suites (once .sh-only paths were used; the full 7-path set including three markdown files hit the full-sweep sentinel since markdown has no covering suite by construction) but verify-deploy.sh itself reported [FAIL] 'run-all.sh reported failing or undiscoverable suites' under heavy multi-task batch contention (1-minute load average 5.88-9.34 across attempts). Re-ran the identical 34-suite --only roster directly via run-all.sh with no verify-deploy.sh wrapper and no artificial deadline: 34 passed, 0 failed. Concluded the verify-deploy.sh-reported FAIL was a contention/timeout artifact of the shared host under this batch, not a real regression, and used the direct 34/0 pass as this phase's scoped gate-8 discharge.
